intro: Tentar means to try, to attempt or to make an effort to do something. It's a regular -ar verb, and you'll use it constantly when talking about plans, learning something or making an effort.

presente.pt: Eu [tento] falar português todos os dias.
presente.en: I try to speak Portuguese every day.
Do you try to learn new words?

presente.pt: Ela [tenta] fazer exercício três vezes por semana.
presente.en: She tries to exercise three times a week.
We try to understand the problem.
They try to arrive on time.

perfeito.en: Did you try to call me yesterday?
We tried to find a restaurant.
I didn't manage it, but I tried!

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I used to try to learn piano.
I was trying to speak Portuguese, but it was difficult.
She always tried to help her friends.
We used to try to have dinner together on Sundays.

futuro.en: Will you try to learn Portuguese?
We will try to arrive early.
They will try to win the game.

condicional.en: I would try, but I don't have time.
He would try to help, if he could.
We would try the new restaurant.

presente.en: Do you understand what I'm trying to say?
presente.pt: Percebes o que estou a tentar dizer?

presente.en: We try to speak Portuguese at home.

perfeito.en: She tried to call me yesterday.
We tried to find the station.

imperfeito.en: When I was younger, I tried to learn piano.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era mais novo, tentava aprender piano.

imperfeito.en: They always tried to arrive early.
You used to try to cook every day.
imperfeito.pt: Tu tentavas cozinhar todos os dias.

futuro.en: I'm going to try to find a solution.

condicional.en: I would try, but it's too late.
condicional.pt: Eu tentaria, mas é demasiado tarde.

notes.presente: In Portugal the ongoing present uses estar a + infinitivo: Estou a tentar (I'm trying). Brazil says estou tentando.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: tentámos (Brazil: tentamos). Tentar = to try; conseguir = to manage. Tentei, mas não consegui.
notes.imperfeito: Tentei aprender português = one specific attempt. Tentava aprender português = I was trying / used to try.
notes.futuro: In everyday European Portuguese you'll more often hear ir + infinitivo: vou tentar, vais tentar, vai tentar, vamos tentar, vão tentar.

compare.en: to try something out / to test

recap: Vou tentar, porque quero conseguir! (I'm going to try, because I want to succeed!)
